identification: French oak A-frame champagne riddling rack (pupitre), hinged at the top with a chain stay. Front board is 6 columns x 10 rows = 60 angled oval bottle holes. Dark weathered grey cellar oak, unbranded. Second (rear) leg board seen only from the inside at an angle: it looks like horizontal ridges/slats, so capacity is either 60 (one holed board) or 120 (both boards holed); not confirmable from the photos. Height looks about 1.5 m (standard pupitre size).

viewing_check: Look at the back board: does it have 60 holes too (120 total) or is it slats? Measure height and board width. Look for any faint stencilled champagne house name or chalk marks (a house name like Moet, Veuve Clicquot or Pol Roger adds a lot). Check the hinge, chain, splits through the boards and whether it stands steady.
